correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=3 and p,q,B>0, concavity of lambda_2 under edge-weight averaging gives an unrestricted value reduction to hubwise constant weights. A complete spectrum factors as z(z-u-v)^(m-1)[z^2-(m+1)(u+v)z+m(m+2)uv]. Unit-gap feasibility is exactly u+v>=1 and m(m+2)uv>=(m+1)(u+v)-1. At fixed sum the cheaper-hub-maximal split is forced when p<q; its cost is strictly convex in the sum, and the solved derivative gives the two exact regimes. Both constructions meet the unit-gap constraints and budget with equality. The multiplicities follow by factorization. The all-parameter proof does not infer an infinite result from finite tests. A standalone stdlib checker passed 72,390 exact-identity, full-polynomial and finite ratio-sweep checks; exact rational high-contrast example m=3,p=1,q=64 has spectrum {0,1,43/40,43/40,33/10}. No asymmetric uniqueness claim is made.

originality.rationale: Ghosh and Boyd (2006) give the general spectral concavity/symmetry framework and graph-family bounds; their nonadjacent-subset construction does not impose two separately priced hub edge classes or derive this two-regime cost formula. Shafi–Arcak–El Ghaoui (2010) formulate generic cost-aware edge/node spectral optimization but supply no explicit two-price biclique allocation in their spectral programs or examples. Shakeri et al. (2015) and the later interconnection study investigate interlayer coupling with unit sum budgets and fixed underlying layers, not the independently priced K_{2,m} design. Targeted public literature and semantic record searches retrieved no explicit all-m result with the threshold sqrt(q/p)+sqrt(p/q)=m^2-2. The elementary spectral framework is prior work, but the explicit price-induced phase and Fiedler multiplicity transition are not consequences of a statement verified in the inspected primary texts. Residual risks are acknowledged; failed searches are not uniqueness proofs.
residual_risks: Historical specialist literature may state the priced K_{2,m} allocation in dual, graph-embedding, inverse-cost or other equivalent formulations not returned by sampled searches.

value.rationale: A fixed complete bipartite K_{2,m} graph with arbitrary independent weights and two positive hubwise cost classes is a natural network-design problem for continuous-time consensus. The exact formula solves an O(m)-variable concave eigenvalue maximization for every m>=3 and budget with an explicit strictly positive allocation. The structural price threshold changes the tight spectral modes, and for unequal prices changes the Fiedler multiplicity from m to one. The critical price ratio grows on the order of m^4, so this identifies a meaningful regime of extreme cost asymmetry where the optimal bottleneck switches. This is not a routine substitution into an existing quoted closed form.
